text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.76% today, continuing a sharp five-day rally that has pushed the stock up 5.1% since late August. The gain reflects a spike in oil prices—Brent crude is now above $95 per barrel—driven by escalating military tensions in the Middle East. Iran has retaliated against U.S. strikes with attacks on Gulf allies, and there are claims of tanker damage near the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint through which 17 million barrels of oil transit daily. For an oil producer, higher crude prices directly boost profits.

The broader energy backdrop is also shifting in favor of producers. The U.S. is simultaneously pushing to expand oil supply from Venezuela through major new concessions and investment commitments, signaling policy support for increased global oil production. This combination—geopolitical supply risk pushing prices up in the near term, plus longer-term production deals coming online—creates a favorable environment for established oil companies like ConocoPhillips.
